sentences.text: DIPAK RAMCHANDRA MAJMUDAR....Respondent(s)

==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR NJ SHAH, APP for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR MD MODI, ADVOCATE for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE VIPUL M. PANCHOLI State Of Gujarat - Thro' J A Shah vs Dipak Ramchandra Majmudar on 22 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95250290/
1  Date : 22/01/2016
ORAL JUDGMENT HC-NIC Page 1 of 5 Created On Tue Jan 26 02:23:59 IST 2016 R/CR.RA/446/2011 JUDGMENT 1.

By way of this application, the State has challenged the order dated 12.4.2010 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhavnagar passed below application Exh.16 in Criminal Case No.4336 of 2009 by which learned Magistrate has discharged the respondent-accused while exercising the powers under Section 245(2) of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
2. Heard learned APP Mr.Shah for the applicant-State of Gujarat.
Learned APP submitted that on 15.5.2009, Food Inspector visited the shop of the respondent-accused along with panchas.
The respondent-accused was carrying on the business in the name and style of Gujarat Juice situated at Bhavnagar.
Accused was present there.

The Food Inspector, after following procedure prescribed under the Prevention of Food Adulteration and rules framed thereunder, took the samples, one sample was forwarded to the public analyst, Rajkot and two bags of the samples were sent to the Local Health Authority for analysis who has given the opinion in his report dated 18.6.2009 that the samples of Mango Milk Shake is adulterated and the same is in contravention of Rule 29 of the Prevention of The Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.

entities.text: Prevention of The Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Food Inspector thereafter obtained the consent from the competent authority for filing the HC-NIC Page 2 of 5 Created On Tue Jan 26 02:23:59 IST 2016 R/CR.RA/446/2011 JUDGMENT complaint against the respondent-accused.
Accordingly, the complaint being Criminal Case No.4336 of 2009 came to be filed.
At this stage, learned APP submitted that the respondent-accused filed an application Exh.16 under Section 245(2) of the Code for discharging him from the aforesaid case.
Learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhavnagar by the impugned order discharged the accused.
The applicant-State has therefore preferred this application.

3. Learned APP mainly contended that the trial Court has wrongly discharged the respondent-accused from the charges levelled against him only relying upon the report given by the Central Food Laboratory.
In fact, as per the complaint filed against the respondent-accused, the respondent was not even having licence for selling the Mango Milk Shake.

Even the report of the local public analyst suggests that the sample of Mango Milk Shake collected from the shop of the respondent-accused was not as per the prescribed standards and it was adulterated.

Thus, there is sufficient evidence against the respondent-accused for conducting the trial against him and,
therefore, at the initial stage, learned Chief Judicial Magistrate ought not to have exercised the powers under Section 245(2) of the Code and, therefore, the impugned order be HC-NIC Page 3 of 5 Created On Tue Jan 26 02:23:59 IST 2016 R/CR.RA/446/2011 JUDGMENT quashed and set aside.
4. I have considered the submissions canvassed on behalf of learned APP.
I have also gone through the material produced on record.

It emerges from the record that after the complaint was filed, the respondent-accused submitted an application for sending sample of Mango Milk Shake to the Central Food Laboratory for necessary analysis.

The trial Court passed the appropriate order State Of Gujarat - Thro' J A Shah vs Dipak Ramchandra Majmudar on 22 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95250290/
2 whereby one of the samples was called for from the Local Health Authority which was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for its analysis.

entities.text: State Of Gujarat - Thro' J A Shah vs Dipak Ramchandra Majmudar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the report submitted by the Central Food Laboratory, the sample was as per the standard prescribed under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

Thus, in view of the report of Central Food Laboratory Exh.12, when the sample was as per the prescribed standard, there is no question of committing the offence alleged against the respondent-accused.

Further, in view of the provisions contained in Section 13(3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, the certificate issued by the Director of Central Food Laboratory shall supersede the report given by the public analysis under sub-section (1) of Section 13.

Thus, in view of the aforesaid provision, learned Chief Judicial Magistrate has rightly exercised the powers under Section 245(2) HC-NIC Page 4 of 5 Created On Tue Jan 26 02:23:59 IST 2016 R/CR.RA/446/2011 JUDGMENT of the Code by discharging the respondent- accused.
In the opinion of this Court, no illegality is committed by the trial court.
Even the scope of revisional jurisdiction is limited as per the settled legal position and therefore I am not inclined to exercise revisional jurisdiction in favour of the applicant-state.

Accordingly, this application fails and,
therefore, dismissed.
Rule is discharged.
R & P be sent back forthwith.

(VIPUL M. PANCHOLI, J.) Srilatha HC-NIC Page 5 of 5 Created On Tue Jan 26 02:23:59 IST 2016 State Of Gujarat - Thro' J A Shah vs Dipak Ramchandra Majmudar on 22 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95250290/
